P1.evidence: Opened by acknowledging the application — 'I saw you left some information, the application. However, I'm an old school guy' — after handling a scheduling failure the prospect raised in the first thirty seconds. The frame ran three parts of four: 'I would love to get in detail, like what's going on right now, with your fitness, with your health, and where you're trying to get to. And if there's a way that we can help you getting there.' Nothing about what is in the way, and no agreement question. The open question was clean: 'Brief me in, like in terms of, first of all, like what you want to achieve.'

P2.evidence: Height was asked, after a fashion — 'But you're tall, right?' produced 188 cm — while age and weight were volunteered. Work was covered properly and probed twice, including the crucial isolating question at 00:11:25 and the desk-bound check 'you probably sit a lot, right?' Health conditions were half-covered: the rep did the difficult and correct thing of raising the suicidal ideation from the application directly, but never asked a general conditions question, so the IBS, the slow bowel transit, the bulimia, the autism and the PTSD all arrived because the prospect volunteered them, two of them prefaced with 'Two things that I forgot to tell you'. Injuries were never asked at all — the slipped disc at 19 that started the whole weight gain came out unprompted. Sleep and energy were never asked, and the two weeks of insomnia surfaced only at 00:43:37 as part of an objection.

P3.evidence: The reflect-back is the best example of the move anywhere in this batch: 'correct me if I'm wrong, that it's not only about losing some extra weight or getting in shape, you're literally fighting for your life right now, for a better life' — answered with 'Yeah, for a better life. I think that's a better way of saying it.' He also drove through to identity and longevity properly. But the ladder underneath it was never climbed: no aesthetics-and-function question, no mobility-versus-strength-versus-energy, no what-can't-you-do-physically, and no 'who else does that impact', which on a call featuring a boyfriend recovering from an assault, a mother he has cared for since he was ten and a dog he walks 300 km a month with was an open goal. The bridge question that ran was 'Why Trevor? Why us?', which is a fit question rather than a driver question; the depth in this call came from the prospect volunteering his history, not from the rep asking for it.

P4.evidence: The strongest root-cause work in the batch. Rather than accepting the story, the rep isolated the variable: 'Before, when the intermittent fasting was working, did you also work as a manager for 50-60 hours a week?' / 'Yes.' / 'So the only different components are taking care of your mom and like recent other stressful situation?' That is textbook — it eliminated the obvious explanation and located the actual change. He also refused the easy answer on the decline: 'after COVID, your fitness, your health, a little bit declined. Why do you think, what happened? Why did you stop working out?' and then pushed back on it — 'But still, COVID was six years ago' — which produced the real gap in the prospect's own words: 'besides working 50, 60 hours a week, walking one and a half hours a day with my dog, taking care of my mother, there's no more time in a week.' He never asked the open what-have-you-tried question, and never ran the information-isn't-the-problem line, which would have landed badly here anyway — this prospect knows more about his own physiology than the script assumes.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame was run. The prospect supplied the ultimate one himself, unprompted — 'otherwise I'm afraid I will have another blackout. I got a blackout at the age of 21, and in that blackout I tried to kill myself, and I really don't want to go there again' — and the rep's response was to acknowledge him rather than to build urgency on it: 'I would like to acknowledge you for being so honest and open about your situation.' That is scored a miss because the phase did not run, and it should be read alongside a note for the coach: not running Phase 5 on top of a suicide disclosure was the right judgement, and the script offers no guidance for the situation.

P6.evidence: No commitment check of any kind. The rep moved straight from 'Okay. I think I got everything' into the pillar walkthrough. Neither the belief question nor the all-in question was asked at any point, and no verbal yes existed before the offer was presented, which is why the price landed cold against a prospect who had given no signal at all about capacity to pay.

P11.evidence: The call never reached payment and onboarding. The price was named, the prospect immediately established a €200/month ceiling, and the rep disqualified him from the six-month programme — 'with $200 a month, that would definitely be a stretch for us. It's not doable' — and downsold to the $199/month community product, which was not closed either; it was left to be emailed. None of the four steps became applicable, so the phase drops out of the denominator rather than scoring a miss.

objection_plays.detail: The right half ran and the rest did not. He normalised upfront payment, offered a split in principle — 'if you're not in a position to do it upfront, that is fine too... if we could potentially find a way to split that up, we can' — and asked the one open-wallet question that mattered: 'what exactly is doable for you in today and in this specific moment.' He even seeded the number with an example ('if you're going to tell me, like, okay, I have 100 euros every single month that is left. That's not enough'), which got him a hard ceiling immediately. Missing: no isolation first, no SHOULD I / HOW reframe, no cash on hand, no cards, no available credit, no investments. Having got €200 he stopped and disqualified. Given the number, that was almost certainly correct — the open wallet exists to find money that is there, and there was none — but the play itself was not completed.

Triggered clearly by 'I quit my job, so I haven't found a new job yet... if I would start this program right now, then I would get myself in serious trouble.' None of the moves ran — no 'things never slow down', no 'when does it actually become the right time', no 'the only thing you can control is right now'. The rep accepted it and parked the deal. Scored a miss because the play did not run, but running it against a man with no confirmed income after 15 October would have been indefensible.

'I want to take at least a week to think about it' was met with 'No worries at all. I will send you the information on the Primal University via email.' No belief question, no thinking-isn't-deciding, no isolation of what is actually coming up. The downsell was left entirely to an email with no follow-up call booked and no date agreed, which is the one place a play would genuinely have helped and cost nothing.

Psychiatric and clinical fit, and the largest gap in the script that this corpus has surfaced. The prospect disclosed diagnosed bulimia nervosa, autism, childhood PTSD, weekly suicidal ideation against a prior attempt, IBS with confirmed slow transit, and a congenital condition that means he has never felt full. He then asked directly whether the coach has relevant expertise. There is no scripted path for this — not for establishing clinical clearance, not for involving the family doctor and dietitian who are already treating him, and not for what a rep should do when a prospect discloses active suicidal ideation on a recorded sales call. The rep improvised, and his improvisation included the single best moment of the call — 'I would lie to you right now if I would say yes, definitely he has knowledge on that, because I don't know that' — and the worst, which was presenting an intermittent-fasting protocol premised on satiety to a man with diagnosed bulimia and no satiety signal.

Market-structure gap with no scripted answer. The playbook's money play rests on 'most clients pay upfront' on a credit card, and the prospect explained why that cannot work where he lives: 'here, credit card systems work differently than in other countries... you have to actually pay it back directly or with huge kind of interests, and those interests are around 14% every month. So that's why everyone's paying it directly.' The primary close instrument is unavailable across an entire market and the script has nothing to substitute.

Cheaper functioning substitute, the second gap the playbook already records. He is mid-way through a Dutch CLI combined lifestyle intervention with a dietitian, both funded through health insurance, and named a local physiotherapist as the alternative use of the same money: 'am I going for that? Or am I going to my local physician and ask them to give me one-on-one training?' The rep did not address the comparison at all.

notes: Phase 4 was excellent and Phase 6 did not happen, so a price landed on a prospect whose capacity to pay had never been touched — sixty minutes of superb discovery ended in a disqualification that two minutes of budget qualification at the top would have produced. Credit where it is due: he told the truth about what Trevor does not know and he refused to invent a cheaper tier, which is the opposite of what happened on the Tom call the same day. The escalation for a principal is not about this rep: there is no script, no screen and no protocol for a prospect who discloses an eating disorder and active suicidal ideation, and one is needed before the next one of these calls happens.
